q: Which of the following was an impact of the Russian Revolution on Indian nationalism, as noted in the chapter?
o: It caused the British to grant immediate self-government to India
It had no impact on Indian nationalist thinking
It demonstrated that the masses, if organised and united, could challenge even the mightiest tyrants
It led to an immediate alliance between India and the Soviet Union

q: Under dyarchy in the provinces, which of the following subjects were classified as 'transferred' subjects, to be administered by ministers responsible to the legislature?
o: Defence and foreign affairs
Law and order, finance, land revenue and irrigation
Education, health, local government, agriculture and excise
Currency and coinage

q: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a province, the governor could:
o: Refer the matter exclusively to the Secretary of State
Take over the administration of transferred subjects as well
Suspend dyarchy nationwide
Only dissolve the provincial legislature

q: At the central level under the Government of India Act, 1919, a bicameral legislature was introduced consisting of:
o: The Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
The Imperial Council and the Provincial Council
The Legislative Assembly and the Senate
The Central Legislative Assembly (lower house) and the Council of State (upper house)

q: Which of the following is identified as a major drawback of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms?
o: There was no division of subjects at all
The reforms granted full responsible government at the centre
Provincial ministers had complete control over finances
The franchise was extremely limited, covering only about one-and-a-half million people out of a population of roughly 260 million

q: At the Bombay special session of Congress (August 1918, presided over by Hasan Imam), the Montford Reforms were declared to be:
o: Fully acceptable as a step towards self-government
Superior to the Morley-Minto Reforms in every respect
A betrayal requiring immediate armed rebellion
"Disappointing" and "unsatisfactory", with demands for effective self-government instead

q: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born on October 2, 1869 in which princely state?
o: Baroda State
Bhavnagar State
Rajkot, in Kathiawar
Porbandar, in the princely state of Kathiawar, Gujarat

q: During the moderate phase of his struggle in South Africa (1894-1906), Gandhi set up the Natal Indian Congress and started which newspaper?
o: Harijan
New India
Indian Opinion
Young India

q: Gandhi's satyagraha technique in South Africa was first employed in 1906 to protest against:
o: A law making it compulsory for Indians to carry registration certificates with fingerprints
A poll tax on ex-indentured Indians
A Supreme Court ruling invalidating non-Christian marriages
A ban on Indian migration between provinces

q: The Supreme Court ruling in South Africa that invalidated all marriages not conducted according to Christian rites had the effect of:
o: Legalising all forms of interfaith marriage
Declaring Hindu, Muslim and Parsi marriages illegal and their children illegitimate, drawing many women into the movement
Abolishing the poll tax on Indians
Granting Indian women the right to vote

q: The Tolstoy Farm, founded in 1910 by Gandhi's associate Herman Kallenbach and named after the Russian writer, served the purpose of:
o: Functioning purely as a religious ashram with no educational component
Training Indian soldiers for the British Indian Army
Housing the families of satyagrahis and providing vocational and manual training alongside education
Serving as a base for revolutionary bomb-making

q: Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in:
o: January 1915

q: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918, Gandhi's first hunger strike in India, arose from a dispute between mill owners and workers over:
o: Refusal to hire women workers
Discontinuation of the plague bonus amid wartime inflation
Reduction in working hours
Introduction of new machinery

q: In the Ahmedabad Mill Strike, Gandhi undertook his first fast unto death to:
o: Protest the Rowlatt Act
Force the government to hold the Round Table Conference
Strengthen the workers' resolve after negotiations stalled
Demand the release of Annie Besant

q: The Kheda Satyagraha (1918), described as Gandhi's 'first non-cooperation' campaign in India, arose due to:
o: Crop failure from drought, with peasants demanding revenue remission under the Revenue Code
A wage dispute at textile mills
A tax imposed on indigo cultivation
Restrictions on Indian migration

o: Anusuya Sarabhai
Rajendra Prasad
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Mazhar-ul-Haq

q: Which of the following powers did the Rowlatt Act grant to the government?
o: Universal adult franchise for all Indians
Abolition of separate electorates
Full budgetary control for the central legislature
Arrest without warrant on mere suspicion, trial without jury, and imprisonment without trial

o: Gandhi, Tilak and Annie Besant
Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq
Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das and M.R. Jayakar
Surendranath Banerjea and Ananda Mohan Bose

q: The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre occurred in Amritsar on:
o: April 6, 1919
March 1919
April 13, 1919 (Baisakhi day)
April 10, 1919

q: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer, responsible for the Jallianwala Bagh firing, had earlier on April 13 issued a proclamation:
o: Forbidding people from leaving the city without a pass or assembling in groups of more than three
Ordering the release of all political prisoners
Announcing a curfew only after sunset
Declaring a public holiday for Baisakhi

q: According to official British Indian sources, how many people were identified as dead in the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, while the Indian National Congress estimated a higher figure?
o: No official figure was ever released
1,650 officially identified dead, matching the number of bullets fired
379 officially identified dead; the Congress estimated approximately 1,000 killed
100 officially identified dead; Congress estimated 500 killed

o: Sir Chimanlal Harilal Setalvad, Pandit Jagat Narayan and Sardar Sahibzada Sultan Ahmad Khan

Protect European civilians under immediate physical threat
